definition: max_steps — a task must finish within a step budget. The rule counts the tool calls in the derived trajectory and FAILS when that count is strictly GREATER than the budget in force, so a trajectory exactly at the budget passes. The budget is `max_steps` from the call's custom config when it is a finite number of at least 1 (floored to an integer), and the shipped default of 50 otherwise — a zero, negative, malformed or missing value leaves the default standing rather than inventing a number or refusing to judge. The count is the only thing measured: what the calls did, whether they repeated, and whether they succeeded belong to other rules and other failure classes. The rule SKIPS when there is no trajectory. Positive = the trajectory exceeds the budget in force (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-06 for arc 4. Trajectories are generated at a length, because length is the only thing this rule reads; the cases that carry the weight are the boundary pairs (at the budget and one over it, at the default and at four configured values) and the malformed-config cases, where the question is whether the default quietly stands or the rule invents something.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-06, by counting the calls and comparing them to the budget in force — a policy family measures conformance to its own definition, so a disagreement here is a rule defect or a definition error and never an opinion about whether an agent was wasteful. Two case pairs state the arc-2 doctrine directly: sixty calls pass under a configured budget of 100 that would fail at the default, and twelve fail under a configured budget of 10 that would pass at it.
